days.title: Day 1 – Introduction to JavaScript
days.definition: JavaScript is a programming language that adds interactivity to web pages.
days.explanation:
• JavaScript makes web pages interactive and dynamic
• Works alongside HTML (structure) and CSS (style)
• Runs in the browser and on servers (Node.js)
• Handles user actions, updates content, and communicates with servers
days.real_world_example: Used for: form validation, dropdown menus, image sliders, real-time updates, interactive maps, and web apps like Gmail.
interactive_tasks: Store your name in variable and display it

quiz.question: What is JavaScript primarily used for?
quiz.reasoning: JavaScript adds interactive behavior to web pages.

quiz.question: Which keyword declares a variable?
quiz.reasoning: 'let' is modern keyword for declaring variables.

days.title: Day 2 – Variables and Data Types
days.definition: Variables store data values. JavaScript has different types like String, Number, Boolean.
days.explanation:
• Variables: containers for storing data
• Declare with let (changeable) or const (constant)
• Data types: String (text), Number, Boolean (true/false), Undefined, Null
• typeof operator checks data type
• Type conversion changes between types
days.real_world_example: Variables store: user inputs, prices, login status. Data types: usernames (strings), ages (numbers), logged in (booleans).
interactive_tasks: Declare variables for name, age, and student status
Convert string to number and calculate

quiz.question: Which creates a constant variable?
quiz.reasoning: const creates a variable that cannot be reassigned.

quiz.question: What is typeof null?
quiz.reasoning: typeof null returns 'object' (JavaScript quirk).

days.title: Day 3 – Operators and Expressions
days.definition: Operators perform operations on values. Expressions combine values and operators.
days.explanation:
• Arithmetic: +, -, *, /, %
• Assignment: =, +=, -=
• Comparison: ==, ===, !=, >, <
• Logical: && (AND), || (OR), ! (NOT)
• Ternary: condition ? value1 : value2
• Operator precedence determines calculation order
days.real_world_example: Used in: shopping cart totals, form validation, age checks, login systems, and discount calculations.

quiz.question: What's difference between == and ===?
options: == checks value, === checks value and type
quiz.answer: == checks value, === checks value and type
quiz.reasoning: == does type conversion, === checks type too.

quiz.question: What does % operator do?
quiz.reasoning: % gives remainder of division.

days.title: Day 4 – Control Flow: Conditional Statements
days.definition: Conditional statements execute code based on conditions.
days.explanation:
• if: executes if condition true
• else: executes if condition false
• else if: checks multiple conditions
• switch: checks multiple values of same variable
• Ternary operator: shorthand if-else
• Conditions use comparison/logical operators
days.real_world_example: Used for: form validation, user authentication, feature toggles, pricing logic, and game rules.

quiz.question: Which handles multiple conditions?
quiz.reasoning: Both handle multiple conditions differently.

quiz.question: What is ternary operator?
quiz.reasoning: condition ? expr1 : expr2 is if-else shorthand.

days.title: Day 5 – Loops and Iteration
days.definition: Loops repeat code until condition met.
days.explanation:
• for: known number of iterations
• while: unknown iterations, condition checked first
• do-while: runs at least once, condition checked after
• for...of: iterates arrays/strings
• for...in: iterates object properties
• break: exits loop
• continue: skips to next iteration
days.real_world_example: Processes: product lists, user comments, form data, API responses, and game animations.

quiz.question: Which loop runs at least once?
quiz.reasoning: do-while checks condition after execution.

quiz.question: What does break do?
quiz.reasoning: break immediately terminates the loop.

days.title: Day 6 – Functions
days.definition: Functions are reusable code blocks that perform specific tasks.
days.real_world_example: Organizes: form validation, API calls, event handlers, calculations, and modular components.

quiz.question: What are function parameters?
quiz.reasoning: Parameters are variables in function definition.

quiz.question: What is arrow function?
quiz.reasoning: Arrow functions provide shorter syntax: () => {}

days.title: Day 7 – Arrays
days.definition: Arrays store multiple values in ordered list.
days.explanation:
• Zero-indexed: first element at index 0
• Dynamic: can grow/shrink
• Methods: push/pop (end), shift/unshift (start)
• Iteration: forEach, map, filter, reduce
• Search: indexOf, includes, find
• Transform: slice, splice, concat, join
• Sort: sort(), reverse()
• Spread operator: ...array
days.real_world_example: Stores: product lists, todo items, search results, user comments, and API data.

quiz.question: What is array index start?
quiz.reasoning: JavaScript arrays are zero-indexed.

quiz.question: Which adds to array end?
quiz.reasoning: push() adds elements to end.

days.title: Day 8 – Objects
days.definition: Objects store key-value pairs to represent entities.
days.explanation:
• Properties: key-value pairs
• Methods: function properties
• Access: dot notation (obj.property) or bracket (obj['property'])
• 'this': refers to object in methods
• Iteration: for...in, Object.keys(), Object.entries()
• Destructuring: extract properties into variables
• Spread: copy/merge objects
• Object methods: assign(), freeze(), seal()
days.real_world_example: Models: user profiles, product details, form data, API responses, and configuration settings.

quiz.question: How access object property?
quiz.reasoning: Both dot and bracket notation work.

quiz.question: What is object method?
quiz.reasoning: Method is function that is object property.

days.title: Day 9 – DOM Manipulation
days.definition: DOM manipulation changes web page content/structure with JavaScript.
days.explanation:
• DOM: tree representation of HTML document
• Selecting: getElementById, querySelector, getElementsByClassName
• Modifying: textContent, innerHTML, style, classList
• Creating: createElement(), appendChild()
• Events: addEventListener for clicks, inputs, etc.
• Forms: access input values, handle submission
• Event delegation: handle events on parent
days.real_world_example: Enables: dynamic content updates, form validation, interactive UI components, real-time updates, and single-page apps.

quiz.question: What does DOM stand for?
quiz.reasoning: DOM = Document Object Model.

quiz.question: Which selects by CSS selector?
quiz.reasoning: querySelector uses CSS selectors.

days.title: Day 10 – Events
days.definition: Events are actions JavaScript can respond to.
days.explanation:
• Event types: click, mouse, keyboard, form, window
• Handling: addEventListener (recommended)
• Event object: contains event details
• Propagation: capturing → target → bubbling
• preventDefault(): stops default browser action
• stopPropagation(): stops event bubbling
• Event delegation: handle on parent element
• Common patterns: form validation, keyboard shortcuts
days.real_world_example: Powers: button clicks, form submissions, keyboard shortcuts, drag-and-drop, infinite scroll, and all user interactions.

quiz.question: What are event phases?
quiz.reasoning: Events propagate: capturing → target → bubbling.

quiz.question: What does preventDefault() do?
quiz.reasoning: Stops default like form submission or link navigation.

days.title: Day 11 – Asynchronous JavaScript
days.definition: Asynchronous code runs without blocking main thread.
days.explanation:
• Callbacks: traditional async (can cause callback hell)
• Promises: cleaner async handling (then/catch)
• Async/await: syntactic sugar for promises
• Event loop: manages async execution
• Microtasks (promises) vs Macrotasks (setTimeout)
• Promise methods: all, race, allSettled, any
• Error handling: try/catch with async/await
• Common patterns: API calls, timeouts, parallel operations
days.real_world_example: Powers: API calls, file uploads, real-time updates, database operations, timers, and non-blocking operations.
interactive_tasks: Implement retry logic for API calls

quiz.question: What problem do promises solve?
quiz.reasoning: Promises provide cleaner alternative to nested callbacks.

quiz.question: What does async do?
quiz.reasoning: async makes function return a promise.
